prompt:
Role and task instructions:
You are a travel agent that can design travel plans.

User request:
Develop a comprehensive travel itinerary for a visitor going to Seoul. The itinerary should be tailored to meet the visitor's specific requirements and preferences.

Destination: Seoul

Requirements:
- Total Duration: 3 days and 2 nights
- Transportation: Subway and Walking
- Must Have: Gyeongbokgung Palace, N Seoul Tower
- Optional: Bukchon Hanok Village, Shopping in Myeong-dong, Visit to a Jjimjilbang (Korean Spa)

Food Constraints:
- Vegetarian
answer:
# Seoul in 3 Days / 2 Nights — Subway & Walking Itinerary (Vegetarian)

**Base assumption:** you arrive at Incheon (ICN) mid-morning on Day 1 and depart ICN in the evening on Day 3. If your flight times differ, keep the day *order* and compress/expand the blocks at the start and end — the middle day is the fixed spine (Gyeongbokgung → Bukchon → N Seoul Tower).

**Base area recommendation:** Myeong-dong / Euljiro 1-ga (Line 2/4). It puts you one stop from Seoul Station (airport train), 15 minutes from Gyeongbokgung, and walking distance to Namsan cable car. Everything below works from that base.

---

## Day 1 — Arrival, Old Seoul & Cheonggyecheon

| Time | Plan | Getting there |
|---|---|---|
| 09:00–10:15 | Land at ICN, immigration, baggage. Buy a **T-money card** (₩4,000 + load ₩30,000) at a convenience store in the arrivals hall; pick up a SIM/eSIM or WOWPASS | — |
| 10:30–11:15 | **AREX airport train to Seoul Station** (Express 43 min, ₩9,500–11,000; all-stop 59 min, ₩4,150) | Follow "Airport Railroad" signs |
| 11:30 | Drop bags at hotel (early check-in or luggage storage) | Line 4, Seoul Station → Myeong-dong (1 stop) or 15-min walk |
| 12:15–12:45 | Subway to Anguk | Line 4 Myeong-dong → Chungmuro → Line 3 → Anguk, ~12 min |
| 12:45–13:45 | **Lunch: Osegye Hyang (오세계향)**, Insadong — fully vegan Korean (fried "chicken," dumplings, stews), casual and cheap | 5-min walk from Anguk Exit 6 |
| 13:45–15:00 | **Insadong-gil** craft shops, Ssamziegil courtyard; optional tea house | On foot |
| 15:00–15:45 | **Ikseondong Hanok alleys** — restored hanok lanes full of small cafés; coffee stop | 10-min walk east |
| 15:45–16:15 | **Jogyesa Temple** — Korea's main Seon Buddhist temple, lanterns and courtyard | 10-min walk |
| 16:15–17:00 | **Cheonggyecheon Stream** — walk east from Cheonggye Plaza along the sunken waterway | 10-min walk south |
| 17:00–18:00 | **Deoksugung Palace & Jeong-dong stone-wall road** at dusk (₩1,000, open to 21:00) | 10-min walk west |
| 18:15–18:45 | Walk to Myeong-dong | ~15 min via Euljiro, or City Hall → Line 1/2 |
| 19:00–20:15 | **Dinner** (see vegetarian list below — Balwoo Gongyang near Jogyesa with a reservation, or a 15-min walk back to Insadong for Sanchon) | — |
| 20:15–21:30 | **Myeong-dong at night** — cosmetics shops open until 22:00, street-food stalls from 16:00 | 5–10 min walk |
| 21:30 | Hotel | — |

*If you're jet-lagged:* cut Ikseondong and Deoksugung, and go straight from Jogyesa → Cheonggyecheon → dinner. Nothing else breaks.

---

## Day 2 — Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon, N Seoul Tower (the core day)

| Time | Plan | Getting there |
|---|---|---|
| 08:00–08:40 | Breakfast near hotel (ask for **soy/oat milk** — "두유" is widely available) | — |
| 08:45–09:05 | Subway to Gyeongbokgung | Line 4 Myeong-dong → Chungmuro → Line 3 → Gyeongbokgung, Exit 5, ~15 min, ₩1,400 |
| 09:15–09:45 | **Hanbok rental** near the palace (₩15,000–25,000 / 2 hrs). Hanbok wearers enter the palace **free** — often cheaper than ticket + photos | Rental shops line the street by Exit 4 |
| 09:45–10:00 | Enter **Gyeongbokgung** (₩3,000; Nov hours 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:00) | Gwanghwamun main gate |
| 10:00–10:20 | **Changing of the Royal Guard** ceremony at Gwanghwamun — arrive early for a front spot | — |
| 10:20–12:00 | Palace circuit: Geunjeongjeon throne hall → Gyeonghoeru pavilion → Hyangwonjeong pond → **National Folk Museum** (free, inside the grounds) | On foot |
| 12:00–12:15 | Exit the **east gate** into Samcheong-dong | Walk |
| 12:15–13:15 | **Lunch: Sanchon (산촌)** — Buddhist temple cuisine in a hanok, vegan set menus (₩30,000–40,000); alternative: **Veg In (베지인)**, also Insadong | 12-min walk |
| 13:15–14:45 | **Bukchon Hanok Village** — Bukchon-ro 11-gil, the hillside photo spot, Bukchon Observatory. It's a residential area: keep voices low, no doorways/private gates | 15-min walk via Samcheong-dong |
| 14:45–16:00 | **Optional:** Changdeokgung + Huwon Secret Garden (₩3,000 + ₩8,000, **book the garden tour online in advance**), or MMCA Seoul contemporary art museum near Anguk | 12–15 min walk |
| 16:00–17:00 | Return to hotel to change into warmer layers (Namsan is windy and 3–5°C colder) | Anguk → Line 3 → Chungmuro → Line 4 → Myeong-dong |
| 17:00–17:25 | Walk to **Namsan Cable Car** lower station (via Myeong-dong Station Exit 3, uphill ~10–12 min) | Or Namsan Sunhwi bus 01A/01B |
| 17:30–17:50 | Cable car up (round trip ~₩14,000) — sunset is ~17:30 in early November, so you get daylight → dusk → city lights in one visit | — |
| 17:50–19:15 | **N Seoul Tower** observatory (₩16,000, open to 22:30), love-lock deck, Namsan pavilion. Optional: walk part of the way down the Namsan trail instead of the cable car | — |
| 19:30–20:45 | **Dinner** back around Myeong-dong / Euljiro | 12–15 min walk down |
| 20:45–22:00 | Myeong-dong shopping round two, or an Euljiro "hipjiro" alley bar with a veg-friendly snack menu | On foot |

---

## Day 3 — Jjimjilbang, Market Lunch, Departure

| Time | Plan | Getting there |
|---|---|---|
| 08:00–08:45 | Breakfast, pack | — |
| 08:45–09:00 | Check out; **store bags at Seoul Station lockers** (₩4,000–6,000) or hotel storage | Line 4 Myeong-dong → Seoul Station |
| 09:15–11:15 | **Jjimjilbang: Siloam Sauna (실로암사우나)**, Seoul Station Exit 1 — 24h, ~₩10,000–12,000, hot/cold baths, sauna, kiln rooms, sleep hall. Bring or rent the scrub kit. **Alternative:** Dragon Hill Spa, Yongsan (larger, more "theme park," ~₩15,000) | 2-min walk from Exit 1 |
| 11:30–11:45 | Subway to Gwangjang Market | Line 1 Seoul Station → Jongno 5-ga, 1 stop |
| 11:45–13:00 | **Lunch at Gwangjang Market** — vegetarian-safe picks: **bindaetteok** (mung-bean pancake, ask for the plain version, no meat), **mayak gimbap** (rice + pickled radish), **hotteok**. Skip janchi-guksu and tteokbokki unless confirmed anchovy-free | 5-min walk from Exit 8 |
| 13:00–14:30 | **Namdaemun Market** for last-minute ginseng, seaweed, ceramics, or socks (10-min walk from Seoul Station) — or Myeong-dong if you want more cosmetics | Walk or Line 4 |
| 14:45–15:10 | Collect bags at Seoul Station; **tax-refund kiosk** near the AREX gates (bring passport + receipts, refund on purchases over ₩30,000) | — |
| 15:15–16:00 | **AREX Express to ICN** (₩9,500–11,000, 43 min); all-stop train if your flight is later | — |
| 16:00 | Airport — comfortable buffer for a 19:00+ departure |

*Earlier flight?* Swap the jjimjilbang to Day 2 night (Siloam is 24h) and make Day 3 a straight market lunch → airport run.

---

## Vegetarian Food Map (bookmark these)

| Place | Area | Style | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Osegye Hyang 오세계향** | Insadong | 100% vegan Korean — dumplings, stews, fried soy "chicken" | ₩12,000–16,000 |
| **Sanchon 산촌** | Insadong | Hanok Buddhist temple cuisine, vegan set menus, evening folk music | ₩30,000–40,000 |
| **Balwoo Gongyang 발우공양** | Jongno, by Jogyesa | Michelin-listed temple food; **reserve a day ahead**, lunch set is best value | ₩30,000–50,000 |
| **Veg In 베지인** | Insadong | Small vegan café, bowls and pasta | ₩12,000–18,000 |
| **Loving Hut / Plant** | Itaewon, Sinchon, Gangnam | Vegan chains/cafés if you detour | ₩12,000–20,000 |
| **Gwangjang Market** | Jongno 5-ga | Bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, hotteok | ₩4,000–8,000 |
| **Convenience stores** | Everywhere | Veggie kimbap (야채김밥), tofu, onigiri, bananas, soy milk | ₩1,500–5,000 |

**Watch out for:** kimchi and tteokbokki (fish sauce / anchovy broth), japchae (often beef), bibimbap (ground beef), doenjang-jjigae (sometimes meat), mandu (pork), and Myeong-dong street food generally. Temple-food restaurants are the safest, most delicious bet.

**Phrase card** (show your phone):
- 저는 채식주의자예요 — "I'm vegetarian"
- 고기, 생선, 해산물 안 먹어요 — "No meat, fish, or seafood"
- 액젓이나 멸치육수 없이 해주세요 — "No fish sauce or anchovy broth, please"
- 비건이에요 (if vegan) / 계란·유제품은 괜찮아요 (if lacto-ovo)
- 이거 고기 들어가나요? — "Does this contain meat?"

---

## Practical Notes

**Transport:** T-money works on subway, buses, and taxis. Base subway fare ~₩1,400–1,500; you'll spend roughly ₩8,000–12,000/day. Subway is bilingual and signage is excellent — Line 3 is your palace/Insadong artery, Line 4 your Myeong-dong/Seoul Station artery, Line 1 links Seoul Station–Jongno–Gwangjang.

**Closed-day logic (check your actual dates):**
- **Gyeongbokgung — closed Tuesdays** (if Day 2 is a Tuesday, run Day 2 on Day 1's slot and shift everything)
- Changdeokgung & Deoksugung — closed Mondays; Jongmyo — closed Tuesdays
- Bukchon is residential: courteous hours 10:00–17:00; quiet outside them

**Weather (early November):** ~3–13°C, dry and crisp, sunset ~17:30. Layers, a light down jacket, comfortable walking shoes (you'll do 12,000–18,000 steps a day), and a scarf for Namsan's wind.

**Book ahead:** Balwoo Gongyang (dinner), Changdeokgung Huwon tour (opens ~2 weeks out, sells out), hanbok rental (walk-in is usually fine on weekdays).

**Apps:** Kakao Map or Naver Map (Google Maps walking directions are unreliable in Korea), Subway Korea, Papago for translation.

**Rough budget per person (excluding flights):**

| Item | Cost |
|---|---|
| Hotel, Myeong-dong, 2 nights | ₩260,000–400,000 |
| Food (vegetarian, 3 days) | ₩150,000–220,000 |
| Transport incl. airport trains | ₩30,000–40,000 |
| Attractions (palaces, tower, cable car) | ₩40,000–60,000 |
| Jjimjilbang + hanbok | ₩25,000–37,000 |
| **Total** | **~₩505,000–757,000** |

**Rain plan:** swap outdoor blocks for the National Museum of Korea (free, Line 4 Ichon), Leeum Museum (Hannam), COEX Starfield Library, or Dongdaemun Design Plaza — all indoor, all subway-connected.
